display_name: Shafer Vineyards One Point Five, Napa Valley
raw_content:
{
  "hook": "One Point Five is Shafer’s way of saying ‘estate fruit that didn’t make the Hillside Select cut’—so you’re drinking the same Stags Leap District volcanic gravel and 15-point-something alcohol, just without the three-year barrel wait list.",
  "wine_summary": "Shafer has worked the same amphitheater of volcanic-derived, Hambright-series gravel above the Silverado Trail since 1972; the vineyard tops out at 600 ft, catching the late-afternoon heat that pushes Cabernet past 29 °Brix every year. One Point Five is the cuvée they created in 2004 to use the blocks that ripen fully but lack the density required for their flagship Hillside Select. The wine is therefore built for earlier release—18 months in 50 % new French oak instead of 32–36—but still carries the house signature of black-cassis fruit, graphite and 15 % ABV that needs protein or time to stop it from singing falsetto.",
  "terroir_expression": "Western Mayacamas volcanic gravel (Hambright & Toomes series) drains fast, forcing roots into fractured basalt where potassium and magnesium levels are double valley-floor loam; that mineral load shows up as a ferrous, bloody note under the cassis. The site’s 600-ft shoulder sits above the fog most mornings, so daily swing tops 30 °F, locking in acidity that keeps the 15 % alcohol from tasting roasted.",
  "vinification_summary": "Hand-harvested at 29–30 °Brix, given a cold soak at 50 °F for five days to extract color without excessive tannin, then fermented in 1-ton open-tops with daily rack-and-return (a technique that pumps fermenting juice over the cap, softening seed bitterness). Malolactic in barrel immediately after primary to round acid before the first winter, racked only twice to preserve reduction that later blows off as cassis and espresso crema.",
  "food_pairing": [
    "Nashville hot chicken—the high acid and 15 % alcohol dissolve cayenne fat while graphite notes echo the spice rub.",
    "Dry-aged rib-eye with porcini butter; tannin binds protein and mirrors the mushroom umami.",
    "Aged white cheddar gougeres—salt and cream soften tannin edge, black fruit pops against the caramelized cheese.",
    "Peking duck pancakes; hoisin sweetness finds its fruit echo and the skin’s maltose crackling resets palate for the next sip.",
    "Late-night In-N-Out double-double animal style: wine’s body stands up to the mustard-grilled patty, acidity cuts the cheese blanket."
  ],
  "comparable_wines": [
    "Chimney Rock Stags Leap Cabernet — same district, similar gravel soils, slightly lower alcohol, more herbal top-note.",
    "Pine Hill Napa Cabernet — hillside volcanic tuff, comparable ripeness but half the new oak, darker fruit profile.",
    "Stag’s Leap Wine Cellars Cask 23 — neighboring estate fruit, mirrored tannin management, 10 $ less on release."
  ],
  "style_profile": "Full-bodied dry red with saturated cassis, firm gravelly tannin and 15-point-something heat.",
  "cellar_recommendation": "Drink 2025–2032; 60 °F passive cellar is fine—alcohol already gives the impression of age, so further decade is about tannin polymerization, not fruit development.",
  "value_assessment": "Street price 130–140 $. Competes directly with Cakebread Cellars Cabernet ( 135 $) and Quintessa ( 150 $); delivers similar Napa polish with the extra Stags Leap spice at a 10–15 % discount. Worth it if you like the district’s iron-gravel signature and don’t mind the punch.",
  "market_position": "You’ll spot it by the glass at steak-house chains (Del Frisco’s, Fleming’s) and stacked 3-deep in upscale Costco aisles; collectors buy it as weekday wine while Hillside Select sleeps in the cellar, and somms use it to calibrate ‘Napa heat’ benchmarks for staff training.",
  "insider_take": "Most buyers think One Point Five is a baby Hillside Select; it’s actually a different animal—brawnier, more immediate, and built for the check that lands before dessert. If you want silky finesse, spend the extra 80 $ on the Select; if you want a honest snapshot of Stags Leap power in half the time, this is your bottle.",
  "aging_potential_years": 10,
  "drinking_window_min_years": 3,
  "drinking_window_max_years": 12,
  "sensory": {
    "acidity": 3,
    "tannin": 4,
    "body": 5,
    "sweetness": 1,
    "alcohol": 5,
    "color_intensity": "deep",
    "aroma_intensity": "pronounced",
    "finish_length": "long",
    "complexity": "complex",
    "quality_level": "very_good"
  }
}
